answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy deploys capacity-constrained trust routing as a velvet rope admission filter. Active agents issue credit lines signed by an asymmetric cipher, bounding how much transaction flow crosses any edge. An attacker must expend scarce social capital and verifiable counterparty credit per rogue node. However, this structure marginalizes new honest participants and bottlenecks routing volume before throughput can reach its zenith.
